verification.sourceNote: ClaimDesk generic guidance compiled from general UK body-repair practice for AI-assisted damage assessment. Not manufacturer data, not Audatex data and not a repair method. Every suggestion is an unverified estimate for the engineer to confirm or delete; follow the manufacturer repair and calibration procedure for the vehicle.

items.label: Front bumper clips, screws and fixings kit

rules.reason: Bumper clips and plastic fixings are single-use and usually break when the bumper is removed, so a fixings kit is normally needed whenever the bumper comes off.
The plastic guide brackets the bumper clips into at the wings commonly crack or distort when a bumper is pushed in hard enough to need replacing.
The energy absorber behind the bumper cover crushes to absorb the impact and does not recover its shape; it should be inspected and is often replaced after a medium or heavy frontal impact.

items.label: Front crash boxes / crash cans (inspect, replace if deformed)

rules.reason: Heavy frontal damage to the bumper usually means the steel or aluminium reinforcement behind it has taken load; the beam and the crash boxes it bolts to are designed to deform once and are replaced if bent.

items.label: Front bumper lower grille (transfer to new bumper)

rules.reason: A replacement bumper is normally supplied without its grilles, so the lower grille is transferred (and replaced if its clips break).

items.label: Front bumper trim mouldings / chrome strips

rules.reason: Bright trims and mouldings on the bumper are transferred to the new cover; they are often clipped or bonded and break on removal.
Plates and plate holders on the bumper crack easily and are disturbed by bumper work; a replacement plate must come from a registered number plate supplier.

items.label: Front parking sensor brackets (bonded to bumper)
Front parking sensors (transfer to new bumper)

rules.reason: Parking sensor brackets are bonded to the inside of the bumper and do not come with a new cover; the sensors are transferred and their wiring checked.
In a heavy bumper impact the sensors in the impact area are frequently cracked or pushed out of their brackets.
High-output (xenon / laser) headlamps are fitted with washers; the pop-up jets and their covers sit in the bumper and are transferred, and the covers are usually painted to colour.

items.label: Headlamp washer jets and covers (replace if damaged)
Headlamp washer pump and pipework (check for leaks)

rules.reason: Washer jets and their pipework sit right behind the bumper face and are easily broken or kinked when the bumper is pushed in.
Fog lamps are mounted in the bumper and are removed and refitted when it is replaced; replace a lamp only if its lens, housing or mounting is broken.
Fog lamp surrounds and their plastic brackets are weak points and commonly break when the bumper is deformed.

Radar-based adaptive cruise and emergency braking sensors sit behind the bumper or badge; removing the bumper, replacing it or adding paint over the radar area can change the sensor aim, so calibration is required following the manufacturer procedure.
The radar bracket is light plastic or pressed metal; even slight distortion moves the sensor aim, so it is normally replaced after a medium or heavy frontal impact.
Night-vision cameras are mounted in the grille / bumper area and need re-aiming after removal.
The front 360° camera is mounted in the grille or bumper; once it is disturbed the surround-view system must be calibrated so the stitched image lines up.
The plastic undertray behind the lower bumper is often torn or pulled from its fixings when the bumper is pushed in or scraped.
Badges are clipped or bonded and are rarely reusable once removed; grille clips are single-use.
Where fitted, the motorised shutter behind the grille is easily broken and will set a fault code if it cannot move.

items.label: Windscreen washer jets and hoses on bonnet (transfer)

rules.reason: A new bonnet is supplied bare: the insulation, seals, buffers, badges and washer jets are transferred and their clips are usually single-use.
When a bonnet is pushed back hard the hinges bend and the bonnet will not sit flush or latch safely until new hinges are fitted.

items.label: Active bonnet (pedestrian protection) actuators — check for deployment

rules.reason: Some vehicles have pyrotechnic bonnet lifters for pedestrian protection; if they have fired they must be replaced and the fault cleared.

items.label: Bonnet lock / catch and release cable
Air deflectors and seals on the front panel
Headlamp mounting brackets on the front panel (inspect)

rules.reason: The bonnet lock, its cable, the air deflectors and headlamp mountings are carried on the front panel and are disturbed by any work on it.

items.label: Air-conditioning evacuate and recharge (with leak test)

rules.reason: Replacing the front panel means removing or moving the cooling pack, so the coolant is drained and refilled and the air-conditioning is usually evacuated and recharged.
Any work on the radiator / cooling pack loses coolant, and its rubber mountings are commonly split by the impact.

items.label: Air-conditioning evacuate and recharge (with leak test)

rules.reason: The condenser sits in front of the radiator and is usually the first part of the cooling pack to be damaged; if it is replaced or disconnected the system must be recharged and leak tested.

items.label: Air-conditioning evacuate and recharge (with leak test)

rules.reason: A heavy frontal impact usually reaches the cooling pack behind the front panel: the condenser, radiator and fan should be inspected and the coolant and air-conditioning refilled whenever the pack is disturbed.
Damage reaching the chassis leg means the load has gone through the crash box and bumper beam in front of it; these are designed to deform once and are replaced.

items.label: Seam sealer, cavity wax and anti-corrosion materials

rules.reason: Structural or welded repairs remove the factory sealing and corrosion protection, which must be restored to keep the repair durable.
Headlamp mounting lugs break easily; manufacturers sell tab repair kits, and broken tabs on the body side are checked when a lamp is changed.
Matrix, laser and adaptive cornering headlamps carry their own control modules that must be coded to the vehicle and initialised after replacement.
The washer jet sits directly in front of the lamp lens and is often damaged with it.
The surround holding the fog lamp is usually broken when the lamp itself is broken.

items.label: Front wheel arch liner {sideLabel} (remove and refit)
Front wing fixings and bumper-to-wing bracket {sideLabel}

rules.reason: Replacing a front wing means removing the arch liner and the bumper side; the wing fixings and the bumper-to-wing bracket are commonly broken and badges or mouldings are not reusable.

items.label: Front wheel arch liner {sideLabel} (replace if torn)

rules.reason: Arch liners are thin plastic and tear when the wing or wheel is pushed in.

items.label: Door membrane (water shield) and door card clips — {zoneLabel}
Door mouldings / rubbing strip and badges — {zoneLabel}
Door glass, regulator, lock and wiring (transfer to new shell) — {zoneLabel}

rules.reason: New doors are supplied as bare shells: the glass, regulator, lock, wiring and trim are transferred; the water membrane and card clips are single-use and bonded mouldings cannot be refitted.

items.label: Door handle with keyless-entry sensor (inspect / transfer) — {zoneLabel}

rules.reason: Keyless-entry door handles contain an antenna and touch sensor that are easily damaged in a side impact and are model-specific.

items.label: Door hinges and check strap (inspect, replace if bent) — {zoneLabel}

rules.reason: A heavy impact to a door can bend its hinges or check strap, which shows as poor gaps and a door that drops or will not close cleanly.
Surround-view and camera-mirror systems have a camera in the door mirror; a replaced or refitted mirror camera must be calibrated so the images line up.

items.label: Blind-spot warning lamp in mirror {sideLabel} (transfer / replace)

rules.reason: Blind-spot monitoring shows its warning in the mirror glass or housing, which is model-specific and must be matched on a replacement mirror.

items.label: Rear wheel arch liner {sideLabel} (remove and refit)
Fuel filler / charging flap and housing (if on this side)
Rear quarter glass {sideLabel} (remove and refit / replace if bonded)

rules.reason: A quarter panel is a welded section: the arch liner, bumper side bracket, fuel flap and any bonded quarter glass have to come out, and bonded parts are often not reusable.

items.label: Rear corner radar {sideLabel} (remove and refit / replace if damaged)
Rear corner radar calibration (blind spot / cross-traffic)

rules.reason: Blind-spot and rear cross-traffic radars sit behind the rear bumper corners; damage near the corner can move or break the sensor, and any disturbed sensor needs calibration to the manufacturer procedure.

items.label: Sill trim / side skirt and clips {sideLabel}

rules.reason: Sill covers and side skirts have to come off to repair the sill and their clips usually break.
Pillar repairs need the interior trims removed; their clips are single-use and some trims cover curtain airbags.

items.label: Front seatbelt, height adjuster and retractor {sideLabel} (inspect)

rules.reason: The front seatbelt retractor and height adjuster are mounted on the B-pillar and can be damaged by deformation there.

items.label: Side and curtain airbags {sideLabel} (replace those deployed)
Front seat side trim / cover {sideLabel} (seat airbag deployment)

rules.reason: Where deployment is indicated after a side impact, the seat and curtain airbags on that side are likely to have fired; curtain deployment often damages the headlining and seat-mounted airbags split the seat cover.
Replacing a roof skin means removing the headlining, aerial and roof mouldings; bonded mouldings are not reusable.
The sunroof cassette or panoramic glass is removed to replace the roof skin and re-sealed on refit.
Roof rails bolt through the roof skin and come off for any roof repair.
A bonded screen needs new adhesive, primer and usually new mouldings; the scuttle panel comes off and its clips break.

items.label: Camera mounting bracket and cover on the windscreen

rules.reason: Lane-keeping, sign-recognition and many emergency-braking systems use a camera bonded to the windscreen; after a screen replacement the camera must be calibrated to the manufacturer procedure.
The rain and light sensor is coupled to the glass with a gel pad that is single-use.

items.label: Windscreen specification check (heated / head-up display / acoustic)

rules.reason: Heated, acoustic and head-up-display screens are different parts; the replacement must match the original specification.

items.label: Heated rear screen and aerial connections (check)

rules.reason: Rear screens are bonded or sealed and carry heater and aerial connections that are checked after fitting.

items.label: Rear bumper clips, screws and fixings kit

rules.reason: Bumper clips and plastic fixings are single-use and usually break when the bumper is removed.
The guide brackets at the quarter panels commonly crack when the rear bumper is pushed in.
The rear energy absorber crushes in an impact and does not recover its shape.

items.label: Rear crash boxes (inspect, replace if deformed)

rules.reason: Heavy rear bumper damage usually means the reinforcement beam behind it has taken load; it is designed to deform once and is replaced if bent.
The rear plate and its lamps are mounted on the bumper or tailgate and are disturbed by work on it; a replacement plate must come from a registered number plate supplier.

items.label: Rear parking sensor brackets (bonded to bumper)
Rear parking sensors (transfer to new bumper)

rules.reason: Parking sensor brackets are bonded inside the bumper and do not come with a new cover; the sensors are transferred and their wiring checked.
In a heavy rear impact the sensors in the impact area are frequently cracked or pushed out of their brackets.

items.label: Rear corner radar sensors (remove and refit)
Rear corner radar calibration (blind spot / cross-traffic)

rules.reason: Blind-spot and rear cross-traffic radars are mounted behind the rear bumper corners; removal, replacement or paint over the sensor area means they must be calibrated to the manufacturer procedure.

items.label: Tow bar, mountings and electrics (inspect, remove and refit)

rules.reason: A tow bar transfers impact load straight into the rear floor and chassis members; it and its mountings should be inspected and it has to come off for bumper work.
The hands-free tailgate sensor is clipped under the rear bumper and transferred to a new bumper.

items.label: Rear bumper lower section / diffuser and reflectors

rules.reason: The lower diffuser, reflectors and tailpipe trims sit at the impact height of most rear shunts and are commonly cracked.

items.label: Tailgate / boot lid inner trim clips
Lock, wiring, wiper and lamps (transfer to new panel)

rules.reason: A new tailgate or boot lid is supplied bare; badges are not reusable and the lock, wiring, wiper motor and lamps are transferred.
The reversing camera is usually mounted in the tailgate handle or boot lid and is transferred to a new panel.
With a 360° system the rear camera is part of the stitched image and the system must be calibrated after the camera is disturbed.
Power tailgate drives are easily bent when the tailgate is struck, and the system needs re-initialising after work.

items.label: Tailgate glass (remove and refit / replace if bonded)

rules.reason: The tailgate glass is bonded into the tailgate and must be removed for a new tailgate; bonded glass is often damaged on removal.

items.label: Tailgate / boot lock striker (remove and refit)

rules.reason: Repairing the rear panel means removing the boot trim, aperture seal and lock striker; trim clips are single-use.

items.label: Rear lamp seal / gasket and fixings {sideLabel}

rules.reason: Rear lamp gaskets are compressed in fitting and should be renewed to keep water out of the boot.

items.label: Fuel tank, filler neck and lines (inspect)

rules.reason: A heavy rear impact can push the rear panel into the spare wheel well and reach the exhaust and fuel system mounted beneath it.

items.label: Front parking sensor brackets (bonded to bumper)

rules.reason: A broken sensor usually means its bonded bracket is broken too.

items.label: Rear parking sensor brackets (bonded to bumper)

rules.reason: A broken sensor usually means its bonded bracket is broken too.
Any damage to or replacement of the front radar needs a sound bracket and a calibration to the manufacturer procedure before the system can be relied on.

items.label: Tyre pressure sensor (transfer / replace) and relearn — {zoneLabel}

rules.reason: Direct tyre-pressure systems have a sensor in each wheel that is transferred or replaced, and the system is relearned afterwards.

items.label: Valve, balance weights and centre cap — {zoneLabel}

rules.reason: A replacement wheel needs a new valve and balancing, and the centre cap is often lost or broken.

items.label: Track rod and track rod end {sideLabel} (inspect)
Hub, wheel bearing and drive shaft {sideLabel} (inspect)

rules.reason: A wheel strike that marks the wheel or suspension commonly bends the track rod or lower arm and can damage the hub, bearing, drive shaft and ABS sensor.

items.label: Rear ABS wheel-speed sensor and wiring {sideLabel} (inspect)

rules.reason: A rear wheel strike can bend the rear arms or axle beam and damage the ABS sensor.
Exhaust damage usually tears or stretches its rubber hangers and can bend the heat shields above it.

items.label: Deployed airbag modules (replace each deployed module)
Airbag (SRS) control unit (replace or reset to manufacturer procedure)
Impact / crash sensors in the impact area (inspect, replace if damaged)

rules.reason: Where an airbag deployment is indicated, every deployed module and fired pretensioner must be replaced and the airbag control unit replaced or reset as the manufacturer requires; nothing can be reused.

items.label: Dashboard (passenger airbag deployment can split the facia)
Windscreen (passenger airbag can strike the screen; inspect)

rules.reason: A frontal deployment involves the steering-wheel and dashboard airbags; the clock spring, facia and windscreen are commonly affected.

items.label: Airbag (SRS) control unit (replace or reset to manufacturer procedure)

rules.reason: When airbag damage or deployment is recorded the pretensioners usually fire with the airbags, and the control unit stores a crash record that must be cleared or the unit replaced.
